**High-signal posts (2026-08-01 to 2026-08-02)**

1. **@xdcaitech**  
   The gap in the emerging Agentic Economy needs new payment infrastructure.  
   @XDCNetwork’s @xdcaitech pairs the open x402 standard with gasless @USDC settlement to let AI agents pay for services per request, without accounts or human sign-off.  
   Read more from the link in comment below

2. **@stakecraft**  
   AI agents can now pay for their own compute.  
   - x402: HTTP 402 revived for stablecoin payments  
   - Solana Foundation + Google Cloud hackathon live  
   - AWS wired it into a quarter of the internet  
   - Settlement in USDC, no accounts needed  
   **Date:** 2026-08-01  
   **Engagement:** Likes=13, Retweets=4, Replies=1

3. **@AemulusAI**  
   Aemulus has an MCP server, which means any AI agent can call your skills directly.  
   Claude, Cursor, whatever you use. Point it at the endpoint with an API key and the whole marketplace becomes callable tools: list the skills, run one, fetch the result, verify the receipt.  
   The agent asks for a skill, Aemulus drives a real browser through the task, and the agent gets the result back with proof of what happened attached.  
   Agents are good at deciding what to do and bad at clicking through a website that wants a login. This hands them the part they're bad at, and it hands them evidence rather than a claim.  
   Setup is one block of JSON.  
   **Date:** 2026-08-01  
   **Engagement:** Likes=16, Retweets=9, Replies=0  
   **Link:** https://x.com/AemulusAI/status/2083702819924672517

4. **@Dafakwu**  
   x402 gave agents the ability to pay for things………..  
   Nobody checks if they’re paying for the right thing.  
   Until now.  
   It’s clean, punchy, and perfectly captures the problem → solution vibe of the original post.  
   A couple of sharper alternatives if you want something shorter:  
   • AI agents can now spend money. @Chance_ makes sure they don’t waste it.  
   • Settlement is irreversible. Verification has to come first.

6. **@web3l0var**  
   4/6) For AI agents the same identity layer becomes foundational. Agents can operate with on chain addresses that carry reputation and payment capability under the 8004 and x402 protocols.  
   **Date:** 2026-08-01  
   **Engagement:** Likes=0, Retweets=0, Replies=1

7. **@Dpw_Jules**  
   When I first came across x402, what caught my attention was how easily it lets AI agents make payments online. It felt like a missing piece for the agent economy, allowing software to pay for APIs, data, and digital services without the usual friction.  
   But the more I thought about it, the more I realized payments are only one side of the equation.  
   If an AI agent is sending money to your business, wouldn’t you also want to know who’s behind it?  
   That’s exactly where @Concordium comes in.  
   x402 is designed to make internet-native payments seamless, while identity is intentionally left outside its scope. Concordium complements that by giving AI agents a way to prove they represent a verified person or organization through Protocol-Level Identity and Zero-Knowledge Proofs, without exposing sensitive information.  
   To me, that’s what makes the combination so compelling.  
   One solves how AI agents exchange value, while the other helps establish trust in who’s initiating those transactions.  
   As agentic commerce grows, I believe payments and verifiable identity will go hand in hand. Businesses won’t just want fast transactions they’ll want confidence in who they’re transacting with.  
   #ConcordiumAmbassador
